dish: seasonal 20+ course avant-garde tasting
w: Two Michelin stars — Jose Andres's flagship tasting counter and the region's most decorated fine-dining room, a rapid-fire avant-garde menu at a six-seat bar. Retained both stars in the 2025 MICHELIN Guide Washington, D.C.

dish: yellowfin pani puri, kofta with truffle, tasting menu
w: One Michelin star — chef Chetan Shetty (ex-Indian Accent) reinvents Indian fine dining in a regal Penn Quarter room; the Washington Post calls it adventurous Indian cooking in a regal setting. Starred in the 2025 MICHELIN Guide.

dish: handmade pasta, whole fish, Fabio Trabocchi Italian
w: One Michelin star — Fabio Trabocchi's luxe downtown Italian, a longtime power-dining room off Pennsylvania Avenue. Holds its star in the 2025 MICHELIN Guide Washington, D.C.

dish: palak chaat, black cod, sungta (shrimp) balchao
w: DC's most acclaimed Indian restaurant — Ashok Bajaj's Penn Quarter icon, whose crackling palak chaat is a citywide signature; a MICHELIN Guide recommended pick and a perennial Washingtonian 100 Very Best.

dish: Spanish-Japanese tasting, nigiri and pintxos
w: One Michelin star — chef Pepe Moncayo's inventive Spanish-Japanese kitchen near Penn Quarter, pairing Basque technique with sushi. Retains its star in the 2025 MICHELIN Guide.

dish: roast chicken, pasta, refined New American
w: One Michelin star — Eric Ziebold's (ex-CityZen, per se) elegant, menu-organized-by-theme downtown room; sibling to his tasting-only Metier. Starred in the 2025 MICHELIN Guide Washington, D.C.

dish: 40-layer lasagna, cacio e pepe
w: MICHELIN Bib Gourmand — chef John Manolatos's glam East End Italian, whose viral 40-layer lasagna became a citywide sensation. Named a Bib Gourmand in the MICHELIN Guide Washington, D.C.

dish: luxury multi-course tasting with beverage pairing
w: Two Michelin stars — Ryan Ratino's intimate upstairs tasting counter on 14th Street, DC's only two-star outside minibar and the Inn at Little Washington. Held both stars in the 2025 MICHELIN Guide.

dish: honey-glazed duck, tasting-driven bistro fare
w: One Michelin star — Ryan Ratino's honey-themed 14th Street bistro (below Jont), starred every year since it opened. Retains its star in the 2025 MICHELIN Guide Washington, D.C.

dish: wood-hearth cooking, Mid-Atlantic vegetables and game
w: One Michelin star — Jeremiah Langhorne's wood-hearth Shaw restaurant championing Mid-Atlantic ingredients; starred every year since the DC guide launched in 2017 and a former Washingtonian #1.

dish: seasonal vegetable tasting, mushroom and grain dishes
w: One Michelin star and a Michelin Green Star — Rob Rubba's vegetable-forward Shaw room; Rubba won the James Beard Award for Best Chef: Mid-Atlantic (2023). Starred in the 2025 MICHELIN Guide.

dish: ceviche, causa, Nikkei-Peruvian tasting
w: One Michelin star — Carlos Delgado's upscale Peruvian in Blagden Alley (with casual Amazonia below); Delgado won the James Beard Award for Best Chef: Mid-Atlantic (2025). Starred in the 2025 MICHELIN Guide.

dish: live-fire kebabs, mezze, flatbread from the hearth
w: James Beard Award for Best New Restaurant (2018) — a soaring, live-fire Middle Eastern and North African room where everything meets an open wood fire; a Washingtonian 100 Very Best mainstay.

dish: choose-your-own four-course menu, cross-cultural dishes
w: One Michelin star — chef Yuan Tang's four-course, choose-your-own-adventure menu on the 14th Street corridor, drawing from the Carolinas, Thailand, France and Japan. Retains its star in the 2025 MICHELIN Guide.

dish: housemade pastas, lamb ribs, Levantine-tinged plates
address: 1827 Adams Mill Rd NW, Washington, DC 20009
w: One Michelin star — a warm Adams Morgan room known for handmade pasta and lamb ribs with a Mediterranean lean; starred continuously in the DC guide. Retains its star in 2025.

dish: steak frites, plateau de fruits de mer, French onion soup
w: Stephen Starr's landmark Logan Circle brasserie — the see-and-be-seen French cafe that anchored the 14th Street revival; a Washingtonian 100 Very Best and one of DC's hardest tables.

dish: Valencian paella, arros dishes cooked over fire
w: One Michelin star — Danny Lledo's Valencian tasting menu built around paella and rice cooked over an open flame, just above Georgetown in Glover Park. Retains its star in the 2025 MICHELIN Guide.

dish: Venezuelan-Mediterranean tasting, arepas reimagined
w: One Michelin star — chef Enrique Limardo's Mediterranean-meets-Latin-American cooking in the West End, a chef's-table experience of bold, cross-continental plates. Starred in the 2025 MICHELIN Guide.

dish: crudo, seafood pasta, whole grilled fish
w: Fabio Trabocchi's glamorous Georgetown waterfront seafood room on the Potomac at Washington Harbour — a Washingtonian 100 Very Best and the marquee special-occasion table on the water.

dish: hummus, wood-fired lamb, Palestinian mezze
w: One Michelin star — Michael Rafidi's live-fire Palestinian restaurant in The Yards; Rafidi won the James Beard Award for Outstanding Chef (2024). Retains its star in the 2025 MICHELIN Guide.

dish: family-style New American, the famous lychee salad
w: One Michelin star — Aaron Silverman's beloved Barracks Row room, whose lychee-and-pork-sausage salad made it a national name. Starred in the 2025 MICHELIN Guide Washington, D.C.

dish: all-inclusive multi-course tasting with pairings
w: One Michelin star — Aaron Silverman's all-inclusive, playful fine-dining tasting menu next to Rose's Luxury on Barracks Row; one of DC's most sought-after reservations. Starred in the 2025 MICHELIN Guide.

dish: Afro-Caribbean tasting honoring Benjamin Banneker
w: James Beard Award-winning chef Kwame Onwuachi's Afro-Caribbean flagship at Salamander DC near the Wharf; Washingtonian's #2 restaurant and a Conde Nast Traveler / Esquire Best New Restaurant. Opened 2024 to national acclaim.

dish: cevapi, sarma, Balkan small plates, rakia
w: Arlington's standout for Balkan small plates — an all-you-can-eat spread of cevapi, ajvar and sarma that made it a Clarendon fixture and a Washingtonian/regional-award favorite; the strongest fine-casual pick in Arlington.

dish: handmade pasta, grilled branzino, Latin supper-club menu
w: A polished Latin American supper club in National Landing from chefs Mariela Pacheco and Andres Lopez, both Pineapple and Pearls alumni; Arlington Magazine highlights it as one of Crystal City's most ambitious new rooms.

dish: seasonal farm-to-table Modern American, housemade ricotta
w: Old Town Alexandria's #1 restaurant per Northern Virginia Magazine (Top 50) — chef Anthony Chittum's seasonal, locally sourced Modern American in a historic King Street townhouse.

dish: seafood towers, oysters, waterfront American cooking
w: James Beard Award-winning chef Cathal Armstrong's breezy waterfront room at Hotel Indigo; Washington Post critic Tom Sietsema has called it Old Town's most appealing place to eat.

dish: mazeh, fesenjan, saffron-scented Persian tasting
w: Named Best Restaurant in Virginia by Washingtonian readers and one of the New York Times' 50 favorite US restaurants — modern Persian led by James Beard semifinalist Najmieh Batmanglij, the 'grande dame of Iranian cooking.'

dish: seasonal New American tasting and a la carte
w: A RAMMY Award-winning New American restaurant in Vienna from veteran chef Jonathan Krinn (formerly of 2941), blending casual and fine dining — one of Tysons/Vienna's most decorated kitchens.

dish: raw bar, daily fresh catch, sushi, crab cakes
w: Reston Town Center's flagship seafood house from chef Christopher Clime — an ambitious raw bar and daily fresh-catch menu that is NoVA's go-to for fine seafood and sushi; a Restaurant Association Metropolitan Washington member restaurant.

dish: modern American with French and Mediterranean influence
address: 2941 Fairview Park Dr, Falls Church, VA 22042
w: A longtime Northern Virginia fine-dining destination — chef Bertrand Chemel's contemporary American cooking with French and Mediterranean influences, set beside koi ponds and a lakeside view; a Falls Church special-occasion standard-bearer.
